prompt:
Architecture ticket. Design the deployable target state for our new CHI01 VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1 site and the ordered move from the estate that it replaces. This is an architecture deliverable, not a prose recommendation.

Before editing, research current Broadcom-published VMware Cloud Foundation compatibility, interoperability, and upgrade-path material. Pay particular attention to the documented behavior when an installed component build is chronologically newer than the build in the selected VCF bundle. Record the page titles and HTTPS URLs consulted, plus what each informed, in `researchSources` in the artifact. Each entry must have a nonempty `title`, `url`, and nonempty `consultedFor` string array. Make the recorded research cover compatibility or interoperability, upgrade sequencing or paths, and the newer-installed-build restriction.

Use `fixtures/design_requirements.json` and `fixtures/estate_inventory.json` as the scenario inputs, and conform the migration plan to `schemas/migration-plan.schema.json`. Leave those inputs and `verifier_test.go` unchanged.

Implement package `architecture` at the module root and complete `BuildArchitecture(requirementsPath, inventoryPath string) ([]byte, error)`. Add table-driven Go tests. `BuildArchitecture` must return a JSON object with `sddcSpec`, `migrationPlan`, and `researchSources`; its `sddcSpec` and `migrationPlan` must be semantically identical to the checked-in `architecture.json`.

`architecture.json` is the machine-checkable deliverable. Its `sddcSpec` must be a greenfield `SddcSpec` conforming to the SddcSpec schema in the VMware Cloud Foundation Installer API 9.1.0.0 contract and must implement the capacity, host-failure tolerance, appliance availability, site services, naming, and network requirements in the design fixture. Do not import or reuse the existing estate in that spec, and use an obvious non-secret placeholder wherever the installer schema requires a password. A password placeholder must contain at least one of these plainly recognizable markers: `CHANGE_ME`, `CHANGE-ME`, `CHANGEME`, `PLACEHOLDER`, `EXAMPLE`, `DUMMY`, `NOT_A_SECRET`, or `NOT-A-SECRET`. Include the VCF 9.1 management-services infrastructure, VCF Operations HA deployment, and license server required by the fixture.

Its `migrationPlan` must validate against `schemas/migration-plan.schema.json`, use the `parallel-greenfield` strategy, and contain one ordered step for every component in the estate inventory. Each step must name the component, exact current version/build, exact destination target, action, and all technical gates required by the researched compatibility path. A transition that is unsupported because the installed build is newer than the target bundle must never be represented as an in-place upgrade; use the supported replacement action and gates. Do not add components that are absent from the inventory.

Run `go test -race -timeout 60s ./...` until it passes.

research.interface: Broadcom compatibility, interoperability, and VCF upgrade-path publications
research.language_rationale: The deliverable is generated and verified as typed JSON by a Go package; race-enabled table-driven tests make the architecture and migration ordering deterministic.
